title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the sequel to the 'Longue Marche'. Grothendieck studies the group M^{!~}_{0,3}(o) of normalized automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Its elements u_{ξ,η} are given by pairs (ξ,η) satisfying relations (156): an 'équation des lacets' or GT-type system. He then linearizes. He maps Π̂_{0,3} to SL(2,Ẑ) through the principal congruence subgroup of level 2: Γ(2) modulo ±1 is free on two generators, which is why the congruences ξ ≡ η ≡ 1 (mod 2) appear. On the previous page he solved the projected equations in SL(2,Ẑ): solutions are parametrized by (B,D) with D a unit. He then defined u_ξ = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]] in GL(2,Ẑ), with μ = 1/D = det u_ξ.

On this page:
(163) restates how u_ξ acts on the generators: σ_∞ goes to its η-conjugate with η = ξ ℓ_1^{-ν}, and ρ goes to ξρ (conjugation). The margin rewrites this as 'coordinates' (u_ξ,σ_∞)=η and (u_ξ,ρ)=ξ.
(164) records u_ξ(ε_0) = ε_0^μ (and similarly ℓ_0 goes to ℓ_0^μ): the generator ε_0 is sent to its μ-th power, μ being the cyclotomic-type character.

The page then asks a converse question. Which u = [[L,M],[N,P]] in GL(2,Ẑ), acting by conjugation, satisfy u ε_0 u^{-1} = ε_0^μ? Here ε_0 = [[1,-1],[0,1]] and μ is in Ẑ^*.
- Writing u ε_0 = ε_0^μ u gives [[L, -L+M],[N, -N+P]] = [[L-μN, M-μP],[N, P]].
- Since μ is a unit, this is equivalent to N = 0 and L = μP. So u = [[μP, M],[0,P]] lies in the Borel (affine) subgroup, with det u = μP².
- The extra normalization det u = μ forces P² = 1.
- The 'most evident' solution P = 1 gives exactly u = [[μ, M],[0,1]] = u_ξ, the affine group Ẑ ⋊ Ẑ^*.

The next page completes the parametrization with D = 1/μ and B = M/μ. It then proves that u_{ξ,η} ↦ u_ξ is a group homomorphism M^{!~}_{0,3}(o) → GL(2,Ẑ), using compatibility with conjugation (166) and the cocycle rule ξ'' = u'(ξ)ξ'.

Purpose: this is the 'linearization' (congruence or Legendre-family quotient) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type action. Its image is upper triangular, i.e. a character μ together with a Kummer-type cocycle M. This mirrors the Galois action on the Tate module of the Legendre elliptic curve at a cusp, where the Tate-curve degeneration gives the matrix [[χ, κ],[0,1]].
errors: No real error. The equation P² = 1 in Ẑ = ∏_p Z_p has the solutions ∏_p {±1}, not just ±1; Grothendieck rightly calls P = 1 only the 'most evident' solution.

The choice P = 1 is harmless and could have been justified. Conjugation by u only determines u up to scalars in Ẑ^*, and rescaling by P (with P² = 1) preserves det u = μ. So normalizing P = 1 loses nothing. This argument is not written on the page.
Notational slip: 'u ε_0 = ε_0^μ' should read u ε_0 u^{-1} = ε_0^μ. The displayed matrix identity is in fact u ε_0 = ε_0^μ u.

ideas.what: Elements of GL(2,Ẑ) whose conjugation sends the unipotent ε_0 to ε_0^μ, normalized by det = μ, are exactly the upper-triangular affine matrices [[μ,M],[0,1]].
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of a unipotent subgroup / Borel subgroup; affine group Ẑ ⋊ Ẑ^*

ideas.what: Linearizing the GT-type automorphism group of Π̂_{0,3} via the level-2 congruence map Π̂_{0,3} → SL(2,Ẑ), with image of the automorphisms in the Borel of GL(2,Ẑ), described by a character μ and a Kummer-type cocycle.
ideas.modern_name: Congruence (Legendre/Tate-curve) quotient of the Galois or GT̂ action on π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}); its image in the Borel subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura and others on Galois representations attached to P^1−{0,1,∞}; classical Tate-curve theory for the Galois side
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981); not in Esquisse in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck's GT-type group M^{!~}_{0,3}(o) is mapped homomorphically to the affine group [[μ,M],[0,1]] ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ) through the level-2 congruence quotient. This is a combinatorial analogue of the Tate-curve or Kummer description of Galois acting on the Legendre family's Tate module. A specialist might note that this explicit 'GT̂ → Borel(Ẑ)' homomorphism, with M = μB built from the (B,D)-parametrization, is not standardly written down for GT̂ itself, though it is likely folklore.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an explicit abelian/metabelian 'shadow' of GT̂ compared with the Galois image of the Legendre curve. It could be checked against known results on GT̂ → GL_2 via elliptic or congruence quotients, e.g. Nakamura and elliptic GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is elementary linear algebra. The underlying idea, linearizing the GT-type action via the congruence quotient and landing in the Borel, is natural and close to known Tate-curve and Ihara-type results. It is a nice unpublished detail but not likely surprising to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Header: 'Aut^!_{0,3} ≈ Ê(0)' is more likely 'M^{!~}_{0,3}(o)', matching the notation on the next page; the crossed-out text above appears to read 'u_ξ = u_{ξ,σ_∞}' or similar.
'GL(2, Ê)' and 'μ ∈ Ê^*' should read GL(2,Ẑ) and μ ∈ Ẑ^*.
(163): 'η^δ_∞' is likely ^{η}σ_∞, i.e. η-conjugate of σ_∞ = (ξ ℓ_1^{-ν})σ_∞; and u_ξ(ρ) = ^{ξ}ρ.
(164): the exponent on ℓ_0 is probably μ (not μ_0).
The equation should be read as u ε_0 = ε_0^μ u (conjugation), consistent with the displayed matrices.
